source: Durian Orchard (ការដាំធូរេន), by Vann Thana Busab and Montry Vong Phanith, published by the Northwest Cambodia Provinces Fruit Culture Development Committee (Battambang), 1998, 59pp, AIDOC code 178-001
text:
Because not every flower that sets fruit will develop into a marketable, well-filled durian, growers should thin fruit in three staged rounds after fruit set:

Round 1, about 3-4 weeks after flowering: remove any fruit that already shows abnormal shape, small size, or uneven/lopsided growth, keeping only the healthiest, most evenly-shaped fruit on each cluster, and thin so that no more than roughly 50% of the original set remains.

Round 2, about 6-8 weeks after flowering: remove any fruit showing insect damage or a cracked/split husk.

Round 3, in the final thinning round: remove any remaining fruit that is small, misshapen, or crowded too closely against a neighboring fruit on the same cluster, keeping only well-spaced fruit with room to grow to full size without touching and scarring each other.

After each thinning round, growers should watch for signs of pest and disease pressure on the remaining fruit, since fruit wounds left by insects or thinning cuts are common infection points.
